evidence: Plaut. Rud. 184b–c: Sequere mē hāc ergō. — Sequor.
terms.comment: With the accusative, of people and of what comes after in time. In argument, sequitur ut … is “it follows that …” (Cic. Fat. 28, Lewis & Short).

evidence: Quint. 1.1.14: nōn longē itaque Latīna subsequī dēbent

phrases.english: Follow me this way, then. — Coming.

phrases.latin: dextrae sē parvus Iūlus implicuit sequiturque patrem nōn passibus aequīs
phrases.english: little Iulus took hold of my right hand and followed his father with shorter steps

phrases.latin: nūbilō serēna succēdunt; turbantur maria cum quiēvērunt; flant invicem ventī; noctem diēs sequitur
phrases.english: clear skies come after cloud; the seas are stirred up when they have been calm; the winds blow by turns; day follows night
